cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to believers scattered across Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia (1 Pet 1:1). He's just told them they've been born again through the living and enduring word of God (1 Pet 1:23). So now he says it's time to clean house.

cards.question: Peter tells the believers to get rid of most of their malice, deceit, hypocrisy, envy and slander.

cards.text: Then Peter grabs a picture everybody knows: a newborn baby. A hungry newborn has ONE item on the agenda, and the WHOLE apartment building knows about it.

cards.question: Like newborn babies, Peter tells the believers to crave pure spiritual ___.
Why does Peter want the believers craving that pure spiritual milk?

answers.text: So they can grow up in their salvation
So they can teach others right away
So they never need help again

cards.question: Peter says these believers have already tasted that the Lord is good.

cards.text: Already tasted it? That's my cookie sample rule, friend: one bite and you're coming back for the WHOLE box. Now Peter switches from milk to building and talks about coming to the Lord, the living stone, rejected by men.

cards.question: Men rejected the living stone. But how does God see that stone?

cards.text: Then Peter tells the believers that they, like living stones, are being built up too. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer waiting for somebody to put me back to work, so if I'm a stone and you pick me for the building, I'm hopping on this gold base yelling, "ME? ME?!"

cards.question: Peter says the believers, like living stones, are being built into something. What is it?
Peter says the believers are being built up to be a holy ___, offering spiritual ___ acceptable to God.
Peter says the believers' spiritual sacrifices are acceptable to God through their own hard work.

cards.text: Peter backs up all this stone talk with Scripture from the prophet Isaiah (Isa 28:16). God says, “See, I lay in Zion a stone, a chosen and precious cornerstone”

cards.question: In that Scripture about the cornerstone in Zion, what is promised to the one who believes in Him?

answers.text: They will never be put to shame

cards.question: To those who believe, Peter says this stone is precious.

cards.text: But for those who don't believe, Peter quotes a psalm: “The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone” (Ps 118:22). Picture the builder who tossed that stone, walking past the finished building every day going, "Nope. Not looking. NOT looking at it."

cards.question: Peter quotes one more Scripture about this stone. To those who don't believe, it's a stone of ___.
Peter says the ones who don't believe stumble because no one ever warned them.

cards.text: Peter adds that this is what they were appointed to. Then he turns right back to the believers with two big words: “But you”

cards.question: Peter piles up names for the believers: a chosen people, a holy nation, a people for God's own possession. What else does he call them?
What does Peter say the believers are chosen for?

answers.text: To proclaim the virtues of the One who called them
To rule over every nation on the earth
To keep to themselves and stay safe from harm

cards.question: Peter says God called the believers out of darkness into His marvelous ___.

cards.text: Out of the dark and into the light? Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, so don't get me started on light, the ovens would go cold before I finished. Peter has two more things to say about these believers.

cards.question: Peter tells the believers that once they were not a people, but now they are the people of God.
Peter says that once the believers had not received mercy, but now they have ___ mercy.

findings.problem: The only card on the end of 1 Peter 2:5 is a true or false that is answered False. No card ever says the sacrifices are acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. A baker who gets it right learns only that it isn't their own hard work, and misses who it is through.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Already tasted it?", the cookie sample line, and "Now Peter switches from milk to building..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The reason the text gives for stumbling, "because they disobey the word" (1 Peter 2:8), is never told. This true or false is answered False, and card 7 tells only "this is what they were appointed to." The baker never learns why the text says they stumble.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question asks what the believers are "chosen for." In 1 Peter 2:9, "to proclaim the virtues of Him who called you" follows the whole list (a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God's own possession). It isn't tied to "chosen" alone. Tying it to "chosen" decides how the parts connect when the text leaves that open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It cites 1 Peter 2:9, but that verse was already covered by cards 8 to 10. The card is only a junk drawer joke plus a transition, so it doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Out of the dark and into the light?", the junk drawer line, and "Peter has two more things to say about these believers."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank question gives away its own answer. The question reads "once the believers had not received mercy, but now they have ___ mercy," and the right answer, "received," already appears earlier in the same sentence. The card tests nothing. The rule against giving away answers only covers later choice cards, not the card's own question.
findings.question: Should a choice card be allowed when its right answer already appears in its own question, for example through a parallel line like 1 Peter 2:10? If not, should a rule be added to prep-walkthrough.md?
